newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares end week well up, index at record.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares end week well up, index at record.

text.p: Shares ended the week higher on the Nigerian stock market, surging on Friday again on strong buying and taking the all-share index to a record high, traders said.
The index closed 7511.29 from 7483.35 on Thursday.
"Construction company G. Cappa was the toast of traders on Friday following the announcement of half-year results showing big increase in after-tax profit," one trader said.
The share closed 62 kobo higher at 13.02 naira, advancing by the maximum five percent allowed.
Cadbury remained in demand after its satisfactory 1996 result released last week. It was 60 kobo up at 31.00 naira.
Coca-Cola's local bottler, the Nigerian Bottling Company also finished stronger, adding 50 kobo to end at 41.00 naira.

Despite queues at pump stations for petrol in Lagos on Friday, confidence in oil marketers was unflagging. Mobil added 60 kobo at 59.60 naira, National Oil gained 50 kobo at 56.50 naira while Agip closed 40 kobo higher at 28.00 naira.
Prospects at Union Bank were brighter because of its good full-year result which had made it a hotly-sought after stock, traders said. It appreciated by 45 kobo to end at 11.20 naira.
Conglomerate PZ lost another one naira to 24.50 naira, ahead of other losers because of lack of interest.
Investors were dumping its shares to move into stocks that provide higher dividends, said one dealer.
Uncertainty cost Nigerian Breweries 55 kobo at 14.50 naira. Healthcare firm Smithkline Beecham fell 10 kobo to 7.40 naira, the same as Northern Nigerian Flour Mills which was 8.80 naira.
Traders said they expected the bull run to persist as the condition that precipitated it still prevailed.
Principally, they said investors were shifting to the equities market to make up for falling money market rates.
Besides, good corporate results now expected to be released was another factor giving investors confidence, they said.
